questions.question: 5 boys A, N, M, K and L are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). K is the immediate neighbour of M and L. N is second to the right of L. How many boys are sitting to the right of A?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is based on the **linear seating arrangement** of five boys facing **North**.

**Step 1:** **K** is the immediate neighbour of **M** and **L**. This implies **K** sits between **M** and **L**. The possible sequences are (**M, K, L**) or (**L, K, M**).

**Step 2:** **N** is **second to the right** of **L**. This means there is exactly one person sitting between **L** and **N**, with **N** positioned to the right of **L**.

**Step 3:** Combining the constraints:

• If we use the sequence (**L, K, M**), then **N** (who is second to the right of **L**) would have to occupy the same position as **M**. Since they are different individuals, this is **not possible**.

• If we use the sequence (**M, K, L**), and place **N** **second to the right** of **L**, the arrangement becomes: **M → K → L → (Empty) → N**.

**Step 4:** The only remaining boy is **A**, who must occupy the empty **4th position**.

**Final Seating Arrangement:**

 **1st**
 **2nd**
 **3rd**
 **4th**
 **5th**

 L

 N

According to the arrangement, only **N** is sitting to the **right of A**.

Total number of boys to the right of **A** = 1

The correct answer is **option 1**</p

questions.question: Height of 6 boys M, N, O, P, Q and R is compared. Height of M is less than only Q and O. Height of P is more than R but less than N. Height of no two boys is same. O is the tallest boy among these boys. Who is the shortest boy among these 6 boys?
questions.solution:
Given:

**O** is the tallest boy among the six boys.

The height of **M** is less than only **Q** and **O**. This indicates that only **O** and **Q** are taller than **M**. Since **O** is the tallest, the sequence for the first three boys is: **O > Q > M**.

The height of **P** is more than **R** but less than **N**. This relationship is expressed as: **N > P > R**.

Combining these rankings for all 6 boys, we get the complete arrangement from tallest to shortest: **O > Q > M > N > P > R**.

From the final arrangement, it is clear that **R** is the **shortest** boy among the group.

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 4'**.

questions.question: P is the husband of Q. R is the son of S. Q is the sister of R. How is P related to S?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

By analyzing the relations between the individuals, we can determine the family structure step by step.

1) P is the husband of Q - This means **P** is **male** and **Q** is **female**, and they are **married** to each other.

2) Q is the sister of R - This establishes that **Q** and **R** are **siblings** belonging to the same generation.

3) R is the son of S - This indicates that **S** is the **parent** (father or mother) of **R**.

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 2'**.

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 3 AM and 4 AM will the hour and minute hands of the clock overlap?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The **hour hand** covers 3600 in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 hour = 360/12 = 300

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 minute = 30/60 = 1/20

The **minute hand** covers 3600 in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered by the **minute hand** in 1 minute = 360/60 = 60

The **relative speed** between the hands = 6 − 1/2 = 5.50 per minute (or 11/20 per minute).

__Calculation:__

At **3 AM**, the **hour hand** is at 3 and the **minute hand** is at 12.

Angle between the hands at 3:00 = 3 × 30 = 900

For the hands to **overlap**, the **minute hand** must gain 900 over the **hour hand**.

Time taken = Angle / Relative speed

Time = 90 / (11/2) = (90 × 2) / 11 = 180/11 minutes

180/11 ≈ 16.36 minutes

The approximate time is 16 minutes past 3, which is **3:16 AM**.

Hence, the hands will **overlap** at approximately **3:16 AM**.

**__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** = |60H - 11M|over2

Here, **H** = hours and **M** = minutes.

For the hands to **overlap**, the angle must be 00.

Given **H = 3** (since the time is between **3 AM** and **4 AM**).

0 = |60 times 3 - 11 times M|over2

0 = 180 − 11M

11M = 180

M = 180/11 ≈ 16.36 minutes

The time is approximately **3:16 AM**.

Therefore, the correct option is **3**
